newsitem.title: NICARAGUA: First two Nicaraguans deported under U.S. law.
newsitem.headline: First two Nicaraguans deported under U.S. law.

text.p: The first two Nicaraguans deported under tough new U.S. laws arrived in Managua on Friday from Miami, authorities said.

Antonio Ruiz, an official in the Migration Department at Managua airport, told Radio Nicaragua that two men had been expelled. He said Marco Sergio Rizo had lived in the United States for four years and Rodolfo Chavarria for three.

The expulsions came just hours after a temporary restraining order expired at midnight, permitting the United States to resume deporting immigrants from Nicaragua and elsewhere who have been in the country for years.

Officials of the U.S. Immigration and Naturalisation Service could not confirm the deportations. They had pledged not to resume such actions until a federal judge ruled on a request for an injunction to halt them.
A source in the Nicaraguan Foreign Ministry confirmed to Reuters that the two men had been expelled, but the ministry gave no more information.
The new laws have sown panic among Nicaraguans in the United States, many of whom the U.S. government encouraged to immigrate in the 1980s, when civil war was raging in Nicaragua.
They have lived since in legal limbo in places like Miami, where tens of thousands have settled and raised families.
Rizo and Chavarria arrived in Managua in the morning on a commercial flight from Miami, Ruiz, the migration official, said.

Nicaraguan President Arnoldo Aleman said on Thursday night he would seek talks with the U.S. government on the new laws. They have also caused alarm throughout Central America, where remittances from family members in the United States are a major source of income.
